title: Response to Request for Proposal: Warehouse Management System

content.text: Response to Request for Proposal: Warehouse Management System

Submitted by [ORG_1] to [ORG_2], attention of [PERSON_2], Head of Logistics. Reference: RFP-LOG-2026-07, issued on [DATE_1]. Contact for this proposal: [PERSON_1], Bid Manager, [EMAIL_1], [PHONE_1]. This proposal is valid for 90 days from the submission date of [DATE_2].

[ORG_2] operates three warehouses for sanitary and heating products in [LOCATION_1], [LOCATION_2] and [LOCATION_3], with a combined storage area of around 46,000 square metres and roughly 38,000 active articles. Today, each warehouse runs on a different combination of the ERP warehouse module, paper pick lists and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to balance stock between sites, to offer same-day delivery to installers and to measure productivity in a consistent way.

With this proposal, [ORG_1] offers a standard warehouse management solution that will be configured for all three sites, integrated with your existing ERP system and introduced in three waves over 14 months. The solution covers goods receipt, putaway, replenishment, picking, packing, shipping, inventory and returns, and it supports both the bulky goods typical of your heating business, such as boilers and storage tanks, and the many small parts of your sanitary range.
We are convinced that our offer is the right fit for [ORG_2] for three reasons:
: our solution runs in 41 warehouses of technical wholesalers in Germany and Austria, including two distributors in the sanitary and heating sector.
: 13 of your 14 must-have requirements are met by standard functionality, which keeps the implementation risk and the long-term maintenance costs low.
One partner for software and integration
: [ORG_1] develops the software and carries out the implementation with its own team, so you have one point of contact from the first workshop to ongoing support.
The total investment for licences, implementation and the first year of operation amounts to
net. Details can be found in section 10.

During the site visits on [DATE_3] and the clarification meeting with [PERSON_2] and the warehouse managers on [DATE_4], we gained a good understanding of how your warehouses work today and where the main challenges lie. We summarise them here to make sure that our solution addresses the right problems.

The warehouse in [LOCATION_1] is your central warehouse and supplies the two regional warehouses as well as around 2,300 installer customers directly. It works with radio terminals that are connected to the ERP warehouse module, but replenishment and slotting are planned manually by the shift supervisors. The regional warehouses in [LOCATION_2] and [LOCATION_3] still work largely with paper pick lists, and stock corrections are entered in the ERP system at the end of each shift. As a result, the stock figures shown to the sales team are often several hours out of date.
From the RFP documents and our discussions, we see the following key challenges:
Same-day delivery for orders received by 14:00 is promised to installers in the central region, but the cut-off time is missed for around 9 percent of orders in peak periods.
Picking productivity differs by more than 30 percent between the three sites, and the reasons cannot be analysed because the data is not comparable.
Bulky goods such as boilers, radiators and storage tanks tie up a large share of floor space and require special handling and transport equipment.
Returns from installers are processed manually and can take up to ten working days, which ties up capital and annoys customers waiting for their credit notes.
The annual stocktaking requires closing all three warehouses for two days, which [ORG_2] wants to replace with permanent inventory.

We understand the objectives of the project as follows: one warehouse management solution for all three sites, real-time stock visibility for sales and purchasing, a reliable same-day delivery promise, transparent productivity figures and the switch to permanent inventory. The ERP system remains the leading system for master data, orders and financial postings.

Our proposed solution is the current release of our warehouse management software, operated as a managed cloud service in two data centres in Germany. It is a modular system: [ORG_2] licenses the core modules for all three sites and can add optional modules, such as yard management or labour management, at a later stage without a migration.

The solution is used through three interfaces: a web client for office users and supervisors, a mobile app for handheld scanners and a touch interface for packing stations. All three interfaces are available in German, English, Polish and Turkish, which reflects the languages spoken by your warehouse staff.

The solution runs in our certified data centres in [LOCATION_4] and [LOCATION_5], which are operated in an active-standby configuration. Data is stored exclusively in Germany. We guarantee an availability of 99.7 percent per month for the production environment. In addition to the production environment, [ORG_2] receives a test environment and a training environment. Updates are installed in the test environment first and are only transferred to production after your approval.

To ensure that the warehouses can continue to work if the internet connection fails, each site receives a local fallback server that buffers scans and transactions for up to eight hours and synchronises them automatically once the connection is restored. We tested this concept with your network team during the site visit and consider the existing redundant lines at all three sites to be sufficient.
The core modules cover all the processes requested in the RFP:
: advance shipping notices from suppliers, receipt against purchase orders, quality inspection and label printing
: system-directed putaway based on article size, turnover and weight, with dedicated zones for bulky goods
: automatic replenishment of picking locations based on minimum quantities and forecasted demand
: single-order, batch and zone picking, with pick-by-scanner and optional pick-by-voice for the small parts area
: packing station dialogues, carrier label printing and loading lists for your own delivery vehicles
: permanent inventory with cycle counts, zero-stock checks and counting on putaway
: registration of installer returns, inspection, restocking or scrapping and automatic credit note request to the ERP system
: planned replenishment between the central warehouse and the regional warehouses, including tracking in transit

Bulky goods are a particular feature of your business. Boilers, heat pumps, storage tanks and long radiators cannot be picked like small parts, and they often need a forklift or a special trolley. The solution therefore manages bulky goods in separate zones with their own putaway and picking strategies. Each article is assigned a handling class based on its dimensions and weight, and the system only creates transport orders for employees and equipment that are qualified for that class. Bulky items for the same delivery route are staged in dedicated loading areas, so that drivers can load them in the right order. At your central warehouse, we expect this to reduce the floor space used for staging by around 20 percent, because items no longer wait in the aisles for the loading of the next vehicle.

The solution will be connected to your ERP system through our standard connector, which exchanges master data, orders, goods movements and stock levels via message queues in near real time. The connector has been used with the same ERP release at four of our customers. In addition, we will connect the solution to your two parcel carriers, to the transport management system of your forwarding partner and to the existing conveyor system in [LOCATION_1]. All interfaces are monitored centrally, and errors are displayed to your key users in a dashboard so that they can be resolved quickly.

The solution includes a reporting module with more than 60 standard reports and dashboards, for example on picking productivity per hour and employee group, on order lead times, on cut-off performance and on inventory accuracy. Because all three warehouses use the same processes and the same data model, the figures can be compared directly between sites for the first time.

The following compliance matrix answers the must-have requirements listed in Annex B of the RFP. "Full" means that the requirement is met by standard functionality, "Partial" means that it is met with configuration or a minor extension, which is included in our price.

In addition, our solution meets 37 of the 42 optional requirements listed in Annex C. The five optional requirements that are not covered relate to yard management and to the management of hazardous goods. Both can be added later with optional modules; we have listed the costs as an option in section 10.
We propose to implement the solution in the following phases:
(months 1 to 3): kick-off, process workshops at all three sites, design of the target processes, detailed interface specification and approval of the solution design by [ORG_2].
(months 3 to 6): configuration of the core modules, development of the minor extensions, implementation of the ERP connector and the carrier interfaces, and set-up of the test environment.
(months 6 to 8): integration tests, a full process test with your key users, load tests for peak periods and train-the-trainer sessions at each site.
(month 8): the smallest warehouse goes live first, so that the processes can be stabilised in a manageable environment.
(month 10): the second regional warehouse follows, with the lessons learned from wave 1 already applied.
(month 12): the central warehouse goes live, including the connection to the conveyor system.
(months 12 to 14): hypercare support on site, optimisation of strategies and handover to the support organisation.
We recommend avoiding go-live dates in March, April, September and October, which are the peak months of the heating season according to your figures. The proposed schedule takes this into account.

Before each go-live, the open stock, storage locations and open orders of the respective warehouse are migrated to the new solution. Master data remains in the ERP system and is transferred via the standard connector. Because stock figures in the regional warehouses are not fully reliable today, we recommend a full count of each regional warehouse in the week before its go-live, supported by our consultants and mobile counting devices. For the central warehouse, a count of the picking locations is sufficient, as the reserve stock is already managed by location in the ERP warehouse module. Each migration is rehearsed twice in the test environment, and the go-live weekend follows a detailed cutover plan with defined decision points at which [ORG_2] can decide to postpone.
We have identified the main risks for the project and propose the following measures:
Availability of key users during the heating season
Plan workshops and tests outside the peak months
Agree on a substitute for each key user before the project starts
Data quality of article master data
Start the cleansing of dimensions and weights in month 2
Provide a data quality report every two weeks
Test the interface early with a simulator in our lab
Involve the conveyor manufacturer in the design phase
Involve experienced employees as trainers and process champions
Provide on-site support during the first two weeks after each go-live

The project will be managed jointly by a project manager from [ORG_1] and a project manager from [ORG_2]. A steering committee with members from both companies meets monthly to decide on scope, schedule and budget. We expect [ORG_2] to provide one key user per site with at least 50 percent of their working time during the configuration and testing phases, as well as access to your ERP specialists for the interface work.
[ORG_1] will provide an experienced core team that has worked together on several comparable projects:
: [PERSON_3], 14 years of experience in logistics IT projects, responsible for eleven warehouse go-lives
: [PERSON_4], responsible for the overall design and the integration concept
: two consultants with practical warehouse experience, responsible for process workshops, configuration and training
: responsible for the ERP connector, carrier interfaces and the conveyor system connection
: responsible for test planning, test automation and the coordination of user acceptance tests

All team members are permanent employees of [ORG_1]. We do not use subcontractors for the core team. During the go-live waves, the team will be supported by additional consultants from our support organisation.

Introducing a new warehouse management solution changes the daily work of around 140 warehouse employees at [ORG_2]. Experience from our previous projects shows that the success of a go-live depends less on the software than on how well the people on the floor understand and accept the new processes. We therefore plan training and change management as a separate work stream from the first month of the project.

We use a train-the-trainer approach. Our consultants train the key users and a group of experienced warehouse employees at each site, who then train their colleagues in short sessions of 60 to 90 minutes directly at the workstation. Training takes place in the training environment with your own article data, so that the scenarios look familiar. For each role we provide short work instructions with screenshots in all four interface languages, as well as video clips that employees can watch on the handheld scanners.

We recommend involving the works councils of [ORG_2] early, as the solution records performance-related data such as picks per hour. In our previous projects, a works agreement on the use of performance data was concluded before the first go-live. We provide a description of all data fields and reports that can serve as a basis for these discussions. In addition, we propose to hold an information event at each site before the process workshops, at which the warehouse managers explain the reasons for the project and the expected changes.

After the end of the stabilisation phase, the solution is supported by our support centre in [LOCATION_4]. Support is provided in German and English. Your key users report incidents through our ticket portal or by phone; critical incidents can be reported around the clock.
We offer the following service levels for the production environment:
(warehouse operations at one or more sites are stopped): response within 30 minutes, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, workaround or solution within 4 hours
(important functions are impaired, operations continue with restrictions): response within 2 hours during service hours, solution within 1 working day
(minor errors or questions): response within 1 working day, solution with the next regular release
: Monday to Saturday from 05:00 to 22:00, in line with the shift times at your three sites

Service level reports are provided monthly and are discussed in a quarterly service review with [ORG_2]. If the agreed availability is not achieved, service credits of up to 15 percent of the monthly fee apply, as described in our service level agreement.

The solution processes personal data of your employees, such as user names, log-in times and performance data, as well as limited personal data of your customers' delivery contacts. [ORG_1] acts as a processor within the meaning of the GDPR and will conclude a data processing agreement with [ORG_2] before the start of the project. All data is processed exclusively in data centres in Germany, and no sub-processors outside the European Union are used.

Our information security management system is certified according to ISO/IEC 27001, and our data centres are additionally certified for availability class 3. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, access is protected by multi-factor authentication, and all administrative access is logged. We perform penetration tests on the solution at least once a year through an independent provider and will share the summary of the latest report on request. Further information on our security measures is available on
All prices are net prices in euros, exclusive of statutory VAT. The implementation services are offered as a fixed price on the basis of the scope described in this proposal.
Software licences, core modules, three sites
Managed cloud service and support, year 1

From the second year onwards, the annual fee for the managed cloud service and support amounts to EUR 168,000 and is adjusted annually in line with the index specified in our general terms. Optional modules: yard management EUR 64,000 one-off plus EUR 14,000 per year; hazardous goods management EUR 41,000 one-off plus EUR 9,000 per year.

Payment terms: 30 percent on order, 30 percent on approval of the solution design, 30 percent after go-live of the central warehouse and 10 percent after the end of the stabilisation phase. Invoices are payable within 30 days.

Our offer is based on the following assumptions:
The ERP system remains in its current release during the project; an upgrade would be handled as a change request.
[ORG_2] provides the network infrastructure, scanners and printers at the three sites; we have reviewed your current hardware and consider 85 percent of it reusable.
Master data for articles, storage locations and customers is cleansed by [ORG_2] with our support before the respective go-live.
The connection to the conveyor system in [LOCATION_1] uses the documented interface of the conveyor manufacturer.
Travel expenses are included in the fixed price for up to 160 consultant days on site.

The contract is to be concluded on the basis of the EVB-IT system contract model, supplemented by our data processing agreement and our service level agreement, which are attached as Annexes 2 and 3. Our general terms and conditions can be found at
We would be pleased to present the solution in a live demonstration with your own article data and to answer any questions. Please contact [PERSON_1] at [EMAIL_1] or [PHONE_1].
